recG4mC1e79KaK37p.Bio: Jason Quitt is a Canadian author and researcher of ancient mysticism, sacred geometry and archaeo-astronomy, and the founder of The Crystal Sun. A graduate of the Institute of Energy Wellness who has studied energy modalities, shamanism and Qi Gong since 2002, he has taught and lectured on mysticism, meditation and out of body experience since 2010. His books include Egyptian Postures of Power, The Yosef Codes, Astral Genesis, Gates of the Anunnaki and Astral Experiences. His latest, The Shining Island: Precession, Axis Mundi, & Plato's Celestial Allegory, reads Plato's Atlantis not as a sunken empire but as a celestial allegory encoding the fall of the pole star and the precession of the Great Year.
recG4mC1e79KaK37p.Name: Jason Quitt
recG4mC1e79KaK37p.Role: Author & researcher of ancient mysticism, sacred geometry & archaeo-astronomy

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Reading the Gods as Stars, Not Spacemen", "body": "Jason says his research began more than twenty years ago with Zecharia Sitchin's books, which he pairs with Erich von Däniken's Chariots of the Gods as the root of modern ancient alien theory, before a decade of studying mysticism and symbolism changed how he reads the old tablets: as allegory for cycles of time, the movement of stars and the growing of plants rather than literal history. Chance frames contact stories as the psyche dressing innate powers in whatever form a culture can accept, and Jason suggests that when Egyptian and Sumerian texts say the gods, they may mean the constellations."}, {"title": "Reading the Pantheon as a Map of Creation", "body": "Jason defines the Anunnaki as the children of Anu, god of heaven, and Ki, goddess of the earth, and Chance adds a linguistic link from Anu to the year the sky marks and from Ki to Gaia. Jason then lines the Sumerian pantheon up beside the Egyptian one: Enlil, god of the air, separates sky and earth just as Shu separates Geb and Nut, while Abzu and Tiamat mirror Nun, the dark waters from which Ra speaks his own name and casts the first light onto the Benben stone. Each god, he argues, marks a stage of creation, a teaching from the top down."}, {"title": "Seven Sages and the Turning of Ages", "body": "Starting from the Sumerian claim that seven sages brought wisdom to the world, Chance traces the same number through the seven Rishis of Hinduism, the Big Dipper, the first seven kings of Rome and the seven planets, with Manu and Noah each making an eighth as the figure who closes one age and opens the next. Jason points to the opening of the Epic of Gilgamesh, where the king builds Uruk on the foundation of the seven sages who lived there before the flood, and the conversation turns to the idea that more than one cataclysm may have erased early Neolithic civilizations."}, {"title": "Matching Myths on Both Sides of the Ocean", "body": "Jason sets the Babylonian Enuma Elish, where Marduk defeats the chaos serpent Tiamat and splits her body into earth and heavens, beside the Mesoamerican myth in which Quetzalcoatl and his brother kill a sea serpent and divide it the same way, and asks how anyone can call that coincidence. He argues academic thinking treats cultures as if they may not be connected. Chance widens it to the world age doctrine, noting that the Greek aion, often translated as world, means age, and reading the egg, the serpent coiled around it and the ouroboros as one symbol, with Tiamat's splitting as the egg being cracked."}, {"title": "Measuring the Sky With the Human Hand", "body": "Jason argues the Sumerian base 60 system is written into the body: thirty bones in each arm and hand, twelve ribs, a skull of 22 bones and a spine of 33 that fuses to 26. He describes the ancients measuring the sky with an outstretched hand, which spans 15 degrees, one hour of the sun's movement, and the cubit running from elbow to fingertip. His wider claim is that gods from Sumer, Egypt and the Americas were drawn on a grid of 23.5 degree angles, the earth's tilt, which he says the Greeks are usually credited with finding only about 2,000 years ago."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: The sacred number system of ancient Babylon is literally encoded in your bones. Jason Quitt, archaeosymbologist and author of Gates of the Anunnaki, returns to InnerVerse with mathematical proof that a universal knowledge system underlies every ancient culture on Earth.
fields.Intro Paragraph 2: Jason Quitt, archaeosymbologist, esoteric researcher, and author of Gates of the Anunnaki: Sacred Geometry Keys to the Gods, returns to InnerVerse to decode the case for a universal ancient knowledge system. The conversation covers the ancient aliens narrative reframed through Jungian depth psychology, reading Sumerian and Egyptian texts as allegory rather than literal history, the gods as constellations and the sky as the first written language, the Babylonian sexagesimal system mirrored precisely in the 30 bones of each arm and throughout the human skeleton, the Anunnaki as children of the sky and earth whose hierarchy maps the levels of creation, the solar myth of the dark waters from Tiamat to Nun to Ra, the seven sages and Noah as the same world age doctrine across every culture, the identical cosmic serpent creation myth on both sides of the Earth in Babylon and Mesoamerica, the 23.5 degree axial tilt encoded in sacred idols from Egypt to South America, and the number 1.728 hidden in the texts of the Epic of Gilgamesh and the Hindu Kali Yuga.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Descent of Inanna Hides a Resurrection Code", "body": "Jason walks through the myth of Inanna's journey to the underworld to attend the funeral of the Bull of Heaven, tying it to the number 72, since three days and three nights repeats everywhere from the winter solstice to Lazarus and the resurrection of Jesus. She passes seven gates and is hung on a meat hook as a corpse, and her husband Dumuzi begs the sun god Utu to turn him into a serpent so he can escape the underworld's demons, the same escape Jason connects to Noah's ark and Vishnu reclining on a serpent boat."}, {"title": "Divining the Cosmos From a Bag of Bones", "body": "When Chance suggests the ancients' numbers may have been fitted to the cosmos after the fact, Jason answers that the Sumerian base 60 system still divides our seconds, minutes, days, months and years, unchanged. It took hold, he argues, because the human body is the measure of the universe, and he reads Golgotha, the place of the skull, as the line and cross marked on top of our heads. He ties this to casting lots, a bag of bones thrown and read, while Chance describes divination as finding a pattern in the microcosm that must hold in the macrocosm, a system he thinks the tarot's major arcana perfected."}, {"title": "A Cow Hymn That Measures the Moon", "body": "Jason unpacks the 4,000 year old Sumerian Hymn to the Herds of Nana, a strange poem counting the moon god's heavenly cattle: 39,600 cows, 108,000 young cows, 126,000 white cows. He shows those figures matching real astronomical numbers, the earth's radius of 3,960 miles, the moon's radius of 1,080, their combined 5,040, and the moon's farthest orbital distance of 252,000 miles, arguing the same sequence recurs in the Epic of Gilgamesh and the Sumerian King List as evidence of a deliberately encoded sacred geometry."}, {"title": "Ishtar Is Drawn to the Season", "body": "Using the Seal of Adda and the Burney Relief, Jason shows Ishtar's carved form built entirely on 23.5 degree lines, from her womb to the eyes of the lion beneath her, and through her wings and the angle in her right hand, while her left hand points at 15 degrees, the sun's hourly movement. Standing on Leo with a Virgo shaped mark on her neck, opposite Pisces on the same seal, her whole image becomes an astrological diagram of the seasons, the earth's 23.5 degree tilt rendered directly into a goddess's proportions."}, {"title": "Sacred Geometry Was Built to Last", "body": "Chance and Jason frame the encoding of solar angles into idols as intentional technology rather than decoration, calling it mimicry magic: taking the measured angles of the sun and building them into a solar deity's proportions to put the artifact in resonance with a real cosmic force. They tie this to why the imagery keeps recurring for thousands of years, arguing that civilizations which ritually replicated this sacred pattern, the seed and order pulled out of chaos, generated more longevity than ones that treated the art as free expression."}]
